title: the XLSX value-only editor retains and resolves shared strings with a stable-index dependency guard
decision: retained, implemented in litchi-xlsx and the producer-shape harness
code_state: internal litchi-xlsx source-closure and parser wiring; no public API item, litchi-opc API, unsafe code, or dependency changed
reason_codes: 0657 deliberately left 0602 D2 deferred; the 0667 assignment explicitly dispatches that remaining shared-string admission work
ECMA-376 Part 1 section 12.3.15 requires exactly one internal Shared String Table part, while sections 18.3.1.96, 18.4, 18.4.9 and 18.18.11 define the workbook-wide index and count semantics
the source closure retains the shared part and materializes its Text table once, only after a worksheet parser encounters t="s"
the retained XML bytes are charged to the existing 64 MiB multi-worksheet bound before the selected snapshot is accepted, and parser allocation/text limits remain active
shared-string cells are readable and preserved, while every value-only mutation at such a target is refused before staging so no table index can be removed, added, or renumbered
producer evidence covers medium and dense 40-percent shared-string sheets; an independent 66935-entry witness exercises the large-table path

accepted_evidence.preservation: admission_tests::a_shared_string_part_is_admitted_and_preserved plus the source-backed integration witness verify adjacent numeric edits, shared text readback, and exact shared-part transfer
accepted_evidence.dependency_safety: set, formula, shared-formula, clear, and remove staging paths share the stable-index guard; duplicate, external, wrong-content-type, outbound, missing, malformed, and out-of-range relationship/table cases are refused
accepted_evidence.lazy_materialization: a malformed unreferenced table succeeds for numeric-only worksheet cells; the parser closure is wired through source, owned, stream, fallback, rewritten, reduced-readback and multi-sheet paths
accepted_evidence.resource_witness: a generated table with 66935 entries and 1863181 XML bytes resolves its final index after an adjacent edit within the 64 MiB retained-part bound
accepted_evidence.producer_evidence: bench/producer-evidence.json records the shared-string role as admitted in medium and dense read variants, with 40 percent shared cells and 64 unique entries
accepted_evidence.timing: bench/producer.json records 12 descriptive after-only cases with three warmups and 15 samples from clean commit 2009e7d9c; p95/p50 <= 1.05 is the declared per-case stability floor, with dense open at 1.153 excluded

accepted_costs.read_only_shared_targets: existing shared-string target cells remain readable but cannot be changed because the editor does not author or renumber the table
accepted_costs.retained_part_budget: the shared-string XML is retained and counted in the aggregate worksheet budget even when lazy parsing avoids table allocations
accepted_costs.wider_admission: workbooks with a valid shared-string relationship and valid indexed cells move from relationship refusal to readable admission
accepted_costs.after_only_timing: the timing artifact has no base binary or A/A floor and is not used as a speedup or regression claim

known_gaps.large_table_throughput: the 66935-entry witness is a bounded correctness/resource run, not a throughput study
known_gaps.real_fixture_census: no 0602-style corpus census or paired publication comparison was added in this follow-on
known_gaps.remaining_value_dependencies: pivot caches, tables, query tables, and other value-dependent relationships remain refused
known_gaps.shared_table_authoring: adding, removing, renumbering, or rewriting shared-string entries remains outside the value-only editor

withheld: any registered speedup, allocation, peak-RSS, cold-cache, concurrency, cross-platform, or real-fixture result

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0
